_about: Who owns where people live. Every housing place on the map has an entry here: a landlord, an off-registry arrangement, or not for rent. Rent tiers are the ids in data/week.json (commons 40, mixed 80, corporate 150, none 0 a week). Canon anchors from the World Anvil: the Housing Authority, Public Advocacy's eviction caseload, Bastion as owners' hired enforcement, Crownline contracting with owners but never owning or evicting, Saint Static Arms' three owners. Every name and hook here is a draft by Eko (status: draft) for the next canon handoff to Nib. Roster doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/4Y8jEd8NjboEdymKjwSSxW

absentee.name: Absentee owner
absentee.about: A holding name nobody has met. Nothing for weeks, then a sudden rent hike or sale notice.

slumlord.name: Slumlord
slumlord.about: Present, cheap and counting. Ignored repairs, surcharges, lease threats.

family.name: Family-run
family.about: Lives in the building or next door. Grace on late rent, favors asked, gossip.

housing-authority.name: Housing Authority
housing-authority.about: Public housing and civic paperwork. Forms, waitlists, inspections. The floor when everything else fails.

certified.name: Certified management
certified.about: Corporate-adjacent, contracted with Crownline. Polite automated notices, and Bastion if you push it.

collective.name: Residents' collective
collective.about: The tenants run it themselves. Work shifts, house votes, shared repair costs.

off-registry.name: Off-registry
off-registry.about: No landlord the registry can find. Whoever holds the roofs decides who sleeps there.

estate.name: Family seat
estate.about: Old families' homes. Not for rent.

temperaments.decent: Gives grace, remembers favors, rarely escalates.
temperaments.indifferent: Answers nothing until it suits them.
temperaments.squeezing: Every week is a chance to charge a little more.
temperaments.strange: Something about this arrangement is not entirely ordinary.

landlords.name: Halvard Mercy Holdings
landlords.who: The third owner since 1987: a name on a letterhead.
landlords.hook: The elevators are still under assessment. A tenant who fixes one gets a thank-you letter and a rent hike for the improved unit.

creep.title: Rent adjustment
creep.text: Following a review of comparable units, the rent at {place} is now {rent} credits a week. Halvard Mercy Holdings

landlords.name: Ma Dresk
landlords.who: A dwarf who owns the building and runs the ground-floor fryer.
landlords.hook: Gives a week's grace on late rent, then calls in a favor: fix her walk-in, run a parcel, scare off a debt collector.

missed.title: That's Debt now, love
missed.body: You had your week and you didn't do me the favor. I don't call Bastion. I do tell the whole Fryer. Ma Dresk

review.title: Come and see me
review.body: Two weeks behind. Pay what you can and come down to the Fryer. We'll call it even when you do me a proper favor.

grace.text: Ma Dresk gives you one week's grace on this rent. After that, she calls in a favor.

favor.text: Ma Dresk is calling in a favor: fix her walk-in, run a parcel, or scare off a debt collector. Do it in Downtime before this is due, or pay. Ignore it and the rent becomes Debt.

landlords.name: The Oduya-Venn family
landlords.who: Three generations of shopkeepers.
landlords.hook: Rent includes a shift at the family stall during festival week. Skipping it is allowed, and remembered.

missed.title: From the stall
missed.body: Rent was due Monday. Grandmother says don't worry, then worries out loud for an hour. Come by the stall. The Oduya-Venns

grace.text: The Oduya-Venns give you two weeks, because you're family. Mostly.

favor.text: Grandmother Oduya-Venn would like a hand instead: mind the stall, chase a supplier, or settle a lane argument. Do it in Downtime, or pay. Ignore it and the rent becomes Debt.

landlords.name: Brightlane Residential
landlords.who: A Crownline-certified property manager with a cheerful logo.
landlords.hook: Automated notices. Complaints route to a form that routes to another form.

landlords.name: The South Market Tenants' Table
landlords.who: The residents, meeting every second Thursday.
landlords.hook: Wrenches and Runners can work off part of the rent. House votes post to the tenants' mail.

grace.text: The Tenants' Table gives you two weeks. Come to Thursday's meeting.

landlords.name: Widow Sallow
landlords.who: Has outlived two husbands and a lawsuit.
landlords.hook: The courtyard lamps are never quite off. Rent receipts arrive signed in a hand that isn't hers.

missed.title: Late
missed.body: The lamps noticed you were late. So did I. Sallow

lost.title: The lamps are off in your window
lost.body: Your rooms at {place} are let again. Whoever signed this, it was not the Widow.

landlords.name: Harbor Row Lets
landlords.who: Manages the waterfront homes and Meridian Logistics' crew lodging.
landlords.hook: Housing tied to the job: crew pay Commons rent, and if the contract ends the lease reprices next Monday.

creep.title: Your rent is changing
creep.text: Hi there! To keep improving your experience at {place}, your rent is now {rent} credits a week. Harbor Row Lets

landlords.name: Whoever holds the roofs
landlords.who: Clans and crews who decide, stack by stack, who sleeps where.
landlords.hook: No listings. Units are found by exploring or through a contact, and paid in favors, work or goods, never credits.

landlords.name: The houses of Old Families' Row
landlords.who: Established houses with a carriage house or a servants' wing to spare.
landlords.hook: A carriage house or servants' wing at a Corporate-plus price, by invitation only. Getting invited is a Standing story, not a purchase.

landlords.name: The old families
landlords.who: The households of the great estates.
landlords.hook: Family seats. Nobody rents here; people are invited, employed, or escorted out.

landlords.name: The Bursar's Office
landlords.who: A window in the Registrar's House that never closes on time.
landlords.hook: Enrolled students and staff pay less, if their paperwork is current. Lapse a term and the room reprices, with a form to explain why.

landlords.name: Glassline Redevelopment
landlords.who: Bought the court's freehold a lot at a time; the old owners still live on the ground floor.
landlords.hook: A buyout letter every month. Holdouts keep the old rent, until the next "improvement" puts it up.

creep.title: Improvement surcharge
creep.text: Following recent improvements at {place}, your rent is now {rent} credits a week. Our buyout offer still stands. Glassline Redevelopment

landlords.name: The Keepers of Three Spires
landlords.who: The monastery's keepers, who decide who is admitted and say very little about why.
landlords.hook: Beds for those admitted. Nobody explains the admission, and nobody admitted is asked to leave without a reason they're given in writing.

grace.text: The keepers give you two weeks, and a written reason if they ever ask you to leave.

landlords.name: The Keepers of Three Spires
landlords.who: Staff rooms behind the sacred frontage.
landlords.hook: Keepers live here. Visitors are walked through, never put up.

landlords.name: The holder of the Long Lease
landlords.who: An elven lessor whose lease is older than the street it sits on.
landlords.hook: The lease runs in clauses nobody under two hundred can read. Rent is fair; the renewal terms are written in a dialect that changes.

landlords.name: The Yard Bunk Office
landlords.who: A clerk with a ledger and three keys to every room.
landlords.hook: Bunks rented by the shift. Double-booked more often than not; whoever gets there first keeps the blanket.

creep.title: New rate
creep.text: Bunk rate at {place} is now {rent} a week. Take it up with the ledger. The Yard Bunk Office

landlords.name: Whoever got there first
landlords.who: Nobody's on the registry down here. People hold what they've swept out and lit.
landlords.hook: Rooms are found, not let. Paid in lamp oil, repairs or keeping quiet about the way in.

landlords.name: The Scavengers' Rest
landlords.who: The people who live in the pocket, and decide who else does.
landlords.hook: Ask before entering. Stay by bringing something useful back from the dig.

landlords.name: The Borrowed Roof Court
landlords.who: The neighbors, who share the repairs that keep the roofs up.
landlords.hook: Miss rent and you're asked onto the roof crew, not out the door.

grace.text: The court gives you two weeks, and a spot on the roof crew.

landlords.name: Auntie Pell
landlords.who: An old orc who owns the stair, the landing and opinions about both.
landlords.hook: Residents keep the landing swept and the rail mended. Do your part and she forgets the odd late week.

grace.text: Auntie Pell gives you two weeks. Keep the landing swept in the meantime.

favor.text: Auntie Pell wants the stair seen to: mend the rail, sit with a sick tenant, or have a word with the shop that keeps dumping on her landing. Do it in Downtime, or pay. Ignore it and the rent becomes Debt.

landlords.name: Patchlight Lets
landlords.who: A shopkeeper downstairs who rents the rooms above every shop on the block.
landlords.hook: Rent goes up whenever the shop below has a bad week. Repairs are "on the list".

creep.title: Bad week downstairs
creep.text: The shop had a bad week. Rent at {place} is {rent} now. Patchlight Lets

landlords.name: The Patchkin crews
landlords.who: Goblin salvage crews who built the row out of what the fields gave up.
landlords.hook: Crew rooms first, everyone else if there's space. A good find pays rent better than credits.

grace.text: The crews give you two weeks. Bring something good back from the fields.

workOff.for: a sorting shift in the yards

landlords.name: The Dustwalkers
landlords.who: Travelers who stop here between journeys and remember who was kind.
landlords.hook: Ask first. A tent space is paid in news, water or a hand with the stakes.

landlords.name: The Roadside Rest
landlords.who: A family that's run the last beds before open country for longer than anyone's checked.
landlords.hook: Beds when there is room. Regulars get the room; everyone else gets the floor by the stove.

grace.text: The Rest gives you a week. The stove's still yours.

favor.text: The family could use a hand: ride out to a stuck wagon, mind the bar on a busy night, or see off a troublemaker. Do it in Downtime, or pay. Ignore it and the rent becomes Debt.

landlords.name: Riverbend Worker Housing
landlords.who: Rooms owned by the steelworks and rented to its own crews.
landlords.hook: Homes within reach of the job, for as long as you have the job. A missed shift shows up on the rent.

landlords.name: Patch Roof Row
landlords.who: The residents, who keep each other's roofs on.
landlords.hook: No crown, no landlord's office. Rent goes into the shared repair tin, and the tin is counted in public.

grace.text: The row gives you two weeks. The tin gets counted on Thursday either way.

workOff.for: a repair shift on the row

landlords.name: The Dry Stacks hearth
landlords.who: Sewers Community households who keep the chambers dry and decide who gets one.
landlords.hook: Keep the pumps running and you keep your chamber. Miss rent and you're asked to take a pump watch, not to leave.

grace.text: The hearth gives you two weeks. Take a pump watch while you sort it out.

landlords.name: Juniper Vane
landlords.who: A fixer who rents rooms to the people she hires, and takes a cut of the jobs she finds them.
landlords.hook: Take one of her jobs a week and the rent comes down. Turn too many down and the rent remembers.

workOff.for: one of Vane's jobs a week

creep.title: About your room
creep.text: Room at {place} is {rent} now. You know how to bring it down. JV

landlords.name: Granny Tikka Rattle
landlords.who: An old goblin who owns Third Rattle Motors and the walk-ups above it.
landlords.hook: Late rent gets a week and a look. After that she wants a hand in the shop.

grace.text: Granny Rattle gives you a week and a look.

favor.text: Granny Rattle wants a hand in the shop: strip an engine, chase a customer who won't pay, or find a part nobody stocks. Do it in Downtime, or pay. Ignore it and the rent becomes Debt.

workOff.for: a shift at Third Rattle Motors

missed.title: The shop noticed
missed.body: Rent's gone to Debt. Come down to the shop and we'll talk. Bring your hands. Granny

landlords.name: Halcyon Tenancy Services
landlords.who: A Crownline-certified manager with a concierge desk and very good stationery.
landlords.hook: A "market adjustment" every few weeks. The concierge can't discuss it, but is happy to log your complaint.

creep.title: Market adjustment
creep.text: In line with market conditions, your rent at {place} is now {rent} credits a week. The concierge is happy to log any feedback. Halcyon Tenancy Services

landlords.name: The Wennick boats
landlords.who: Captain Orra Wennick, an orc, and the family that has moored here for four generations.
landlords.hook: Late rent gets you a week's grace. After that, the captain wants a hand on the water.

grace.text: Captain Wennick gives you a week. The river's patient. She's mostly patient.

favor.text: The captain wants a hand on the water: crew a night run, patch a hull, or find out who's been cutting mooring lines. Do it in Downtime, or pay. Ignore it and the rent becomes Debt.

missed.title: Word from the captain
missed.body: That's Debt now. Come aboard and talk to me before the next berth move. O. Wennick

landlords.name: Adyta Housing Authority
landlords.who: Emergency accommodation for anyone who has lost their home.
landlords.hook: The floor nobody falls through. Nobody rents a room here. You're placed in one.

landlords.name: Tallow & Grade Residential
landlords.who: Runs the contractor dorms under a Crownline service agreement. Crownline itself never owns or evicts.
landlords.hook: The rent is tied to the contract. The contract is tied to the whistle.

floor.name: Adyta Housing Authority
floor.about: Emergency accommodation for anyone who loses their home: a real address, a waitlist, no rent for now, and a bad mood. Items and debts come along.

letter.title: Emergency accommodation
letter.body: You've been placed in emergency accommodation while your case is reviewed. You have an address again and no rent for now. Your debts are still yours. Waitlist position: assigned.

_ladder: Missed rent climbs a ladder of letters, one step per unpaid week: 1 missed, 2 review, 3 bastion (a scene hook for the next session, and Public Advocacy's eviction-defense job), 4 lost (the unit goes and the character moves to Housing Authority emergency accommodation; items and debts come along). A type's ladder is how far it climbs: family-run and collectives stop at 2. Paying off the debt to your landlord resets it. {landlord} and {place} fill in.

missed.title: Payment not received
missed.body: Our records show no payment for your unit at {place} this week. Please remit at your earliest convenience. This is an automated courtesy. {landlord}

review.title: Account under review
review.body: Your tenancy at {place} has been flagged after repeated non-payment. A representative will be assigned to your case.

bastion.title: Recovery contractor assigned
bastion.body: {landlord} has engaged Bastion Dynamics to recover possession of your unit at {place}. A contractor will attend. Public Advocacy takes eviction cases: look for Eviction Interference on the Job Board.

lost.title: Tenancy ended
lost.body: {landlord} has recovered possession of your unit at {place}. Your belongings were moved to the curb, where most of them still are.

missed.title: Rent is late
missed.body: Rent's late on {place}. Late fee's coming. Don't make me come up there. {landlord}

review.title: Your lease
review.body: I'm reviewing your lease. That means I'm looking for a reason, and you keep handing me one.

bastion.title: I've called Bastion
bastion.body: I've called Bastion. They'll be round about {place}. Be out or be polite. Public Advocacy takes eviction cases: look for Eviction Interference on the Job Board.

lost.title: Out
lost.body: Your unit at {place} is let to someone who pays. Your things are in the hall. The hall is also let.

missed.title: About the rent
missed.body: Rent was due Monday, love. Come by when you can and we will sort it out. {landlord}

review.title: We need to talk
review.body: It's two weeks now. Come and talk to us before it's three. We'll work something out, but you have to come in.

missed.title: The Table noticed
missed.body: The Tenants' Table noticed rent for {place} didn't come in. Nobody's angry. Come to Thursday's meeting, or put in a repair shift.

review.title: House vote
review.body: Your rent is on the agenda at Thursday's meeting. Come and speak for yourself, or someone will speak for you.

missed.title: Payment reminder
missed.body: Hi there! Your rent for {place} is overdue. A late fee has been applied to your account. Thanks for being part of the {landlord} community!

review.title: Lease Review
review.body: Following missed payments, your lease at {place} is under review. Continued tenancy may require a risk surcharge. This message was sent automatically. Replies are not monitored.

bastion.title: Recovery of possession scheduled
bastion.body: {landlord} has scheduled recovery of possession at {place}, carried out by our partner Bastion Dynamics. We appreciate your cooperation. Public Advocacy takes eviction cases: look for Eviction Interference on the Job Board.

lost.title: Your tenancy has ended
lost.body: Your tenancy at {place} has ended. Remaining items will be held for 72 hours for a storage fee. Thank you for living with {landlord}!

missed.title: A word
missed.body: The household notes that your payment is late. The household does not usually need to note things twice.

review.title: The arrangement
review.body: The household has asked that your arrangement at {place} be reconsidered.

bastion.title: An escort
bastion.body: The household has asked Bastion Dynamics to see you out of {place}, courteously. Public Advocacy takes eviction cases: look for Eviction Interference on the Job Board.

lost.title: Invitation withdrawn
lost.body: Your invitation to {place} has been withdrawn. The household wishes you well, elsewhere.

_terms: Each landlord's own terms (none means none): grace = weeks of grace on a late bill, given only by landlords who would; favor = after the grace runs out, a favor done in Downtime settles the bill (the scene lives in data/downtime.json favors, keyed by the landlord's name); workOff = a standing weekly shift that takes credits off the rent (honor system: the PDA trusts you to turn up); creep = the rent rises by credits every everyWeeks weeks you live there, never past the tier's band in data/rentals.json. {place} and {rent} fill in.
